category_title: High-achieving students who dominate group work and exclude peers in competitive settings
minimal_context: The student is working in a mixed-ability group on a multiple-choice assessment with the goal of achieving high scores on the group test.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please continue working with your mixed-ability group on this multiple-choice assessment to achieve high scores on your group test.

STUDENT: I've already gone through the first section and I'm just giving them the answers so we can go faster. I don't want to be held back by my slower teammates.

TUTOR: What do you think about discussing the questions with the rest of the group?

STUDENT: I always appreciate contribution of all members. However, I have to say I feel safer if the contribution comes from a good student. Whenever we receive products from a less able member, we need to spend time rechecking so it takes our time. When they get stuck, I just jump into their mouth to keep us moving.

TUTOR: The instructions ask that the group works together to choose the answers.

STUDENT: It's a multiple-choice assessment, and I know that eventually I'm the one who makes the final decisions in choosing the right answers for the group anyway. There's really no need to listen to others; we can just go ahead with using my own answers.

options.A: Deliver verbal statements or gestures (e.g., high five, thumbs up) indicating approval beyond simple acknowledgment during the group task.
options.B: Ignore the negative behavior, including verbal actions like speaking out of turn and motor actions like getting out of the seat.
options.C: Use a series of probing questions to demonstrate that the student can apply, analyze, synthesize, and evaluate solutions to the assessment.
options.D: Provide opportunities to respond as a form of tutor attention during the group's multiple-choice assessment.
